actor: cross-orchestrator interop-matrix program manager at the matrix-coordinating vendor (Mistral Workflows)
job: Driving the five-vendor interop matrix to its announced first-week-of-June general-availability target with the five-surface mitigation set as the documented default.
outcome: The five-vendor cross-orchestrator interop matrix ships as a documented GA production tier with the full five-surface signed-load mitigation bundle as default, not opt-in.
motivation: A GA tier shipping with a partial mitigation default would invite an immediate procurement-eligibility objection, and the matrix is positioned to serve all fourteen Indo-Pacific cohort jurisdictions.

task.who: matrix program management plus partner-engineering plus security-mitigation working group across the five participating vendors
task.what: finalize and document the five-tier signed-load mitigation default across all five orchestrators
task.where: the cross-vendor interop matrix specification and its GA production-tier compatibility documentation
task.when: May 2026 through the first week of June 2026
task.why: a partial-mitigation GA default would trigger a procurement-eligibility objection
task.how: four-tier signed-checkpoint plus path-canonicalization plus serializer-canonicalization plus nested-dependency-resolution mitigation pattern

task.where: the Codex CLI v3.1.3 point release and its agent-checkpoint loader path
task.when: shipped Friday May 15 2026, sustained through the early-June matrix GA
task.why: completes the client-side surface so the matrix can default to five tiers
task.how: nested-dependency-resolution canonicalization folded into manifest-allowlist validation

task.where: the vLLM, SGLang RadixArk, and TGI release branches and manifest fetchers
